findings.problem: The frozen contract's signal C is NOT implemented as frozen. `complexityGate.signals.C_enumeratedSteps.detect` (frozen) requires 'C fires when TWO OR MORE of its three independent sub-signals hold: C1 enumerated lines >= 3; C2 distinct action verbs >= 3; C3 action clauses >= 3', i.e. C is a single soft signal with a >=2-of-3 majority. `evaluateComplexityGate` (session-start.js:157-173) instead pushes C1, C2 and C3 as THREE independent top-level signals and lets the flat global count reach MATCHED_SIGNAL_MIN=2, so no majority of C's own sub-signals is ever required. Demonstrated over-trigger: 'Check the test, build the package, verify the output.' yields signals [C2,C3] -> trigger=true — a single ordinary sentence provisions a staged team, and C's own 2-of-3 rule does not hold for it (C1=0). The same shape fires on any list of >=3 distinct action verbs. This contradicts t15's own cannotVerify statement that the sub-rules were kept 'as SEPARATE checks' and makes the comment block at session-start.js:35-38 (which still describes the SUPERSEDED literal '>=3 lines, or >=3 action verbs') misleading. The frozen 3+3 prompt sets still pass, so the two-sided case cannot see this class.
findings.requiredFix: Either (a) make C discharge exactly one signal only when >=2 of {C1,C2,C3} hold and assert that in the offline gate probe, or (b) amend the FROZEN contract text to the flat-count rule and re-freeze it with a new pin. Also fix the module docstring to describe whichever rule wins. Owner: t15's writer (out of my inScope).

findings.problem: OPT-1 is only half applied: the claim path is fixed, the UI/visual surface still treats a FAILED dependency as blocking. `taskVisualState` (state.js:963-978) tests `dependency.status !== 'completed'` for every dependency, so a pending dependent of a failed dependency is reported `blocked` even though `unsatisfiedDependencies` says it is claimable — my matrix shows this in one row. `snapshot.js:105` puts that visual state into the team snapshot the Web panel renders, and `taskContractView`/`renderTaskContract` do not surface `failed_dependencies` either (the field exists at tools.js:2491 but takes an `allTasks` argument that `taskContractView` calls without passing). Net effect: a captain looking at the panel sees the dependent still blocked and will not dispatch it, which is exactly the 'failed dependency pins the downstream forever' behaviour OPT-1 was created to remove; t15's own comment at state.js:106-107 claims the view 'carries the failure so the view can say so', but the view cannot.
findings.requiredFix: Route taskVisualState through the same three-state predicate (treat completed AND cancelled as satisfied, failed as non-blocking, everything else as blocking) and pass the task list into taskContractView so `failed_dependencies` is actually populated; add a falsifiable assertion (failed dep => visual 'open', pending dep => visual 'blocked'). Owner: t15's writer.

findings.problem: Two of t17's claims rest on assertions that cannot fail. (1) A8 'the two-sided case fails when either side breaks' has no reverse control: `session-start-team.mjs --self-test` exercises ONLY the offline predicate, and the real case has no falsification run (e.g. a temporarily disabled gate or an inverted expectation), so 'a gate that cannot fail one side is not accepted' is asserted, not demonstrated. The frozen-contract acceptance line itself demands the case must assert BOTH directions on the same settled revision; it does assert both directions, but nothing proves the case would report failure if the gate regressed. (2) The S3 assertion ('resume across restart') is a source-substring check (`expect(schedulerSrc).toContain("task.status === 'pending'")`) plus an INLINE re-implementation of the readiness filter inside the test (test/s1-s4-semantics.test.mjs:128-142) — it never calls the real `nextReadyTask`, and its inline filter uses the OLD dependency rule (only 'completed'/'cancelled' satisfy) while the shipped scheduler now also admits 'failed'. It is a tautology about a copy, not a run of the resume path.
findings.requiredFix: Add a reverse-control run to the two-sided case (e.g. assert the case's own negative control, as preset-conformance does) and replace S3's inline filter with an import of the real readiness predicate (or a `verification`-kind assertion executed against a restarted scheduler). Owner: verification/QA writer.

findings.problem: The frozen `manualEntryNames.stateDir` is `.mpd/team`, but the plugin's own schema default for `stateDir` is `.agent-teams` (lib/index.js:Config). The bundle patch and the installer self-test pin `.mpd/team`, so the delivered configuration is correct; the latent risk is a consumer that instantiates the plugin without the row override, which silently lands state in `.agent-teams` instead of the frozen workspace root.
findings.requiredFix: Change the schema default to '.mpd/team' (matching the frozen value and the patch) so the two cannot disagree.

findings.problem: The frozen `manualEntryNames.tools` list has 14 names but `lib/tool-names.js` TEAM_TOOL_NAMES has 13 — `agent_teams_task_contract` (registered at tools.js, and present in the frozen list) is absent, so it is excluded from the captain prompt tool list and from the member deny computation. Impact is small (the tool stays callable by everyone, which is benign for a read-only contract surface), but the frozen list and the governed list disagree.
findings.requiredFix: Add `agent_teams_task_contract` to TEAM_TOOL_NAMES (and decide deliberately whether it belongs in MEMBER_TOOL_NAMES), or amend the frozen list. Owner: writer.

residualRisks: Signal C's loosened form (F1) is a recall/precision dial on the ONLY automatic trigger: any list of >= 3 distinct action verbs now stages a team. If the intent is 'ordinary sessions stay solo', the trigger rate should be re-measured after the fix on a normal-prompt corpus, not only on the 3+3 frozen set.

OPT-2's residual reclamation (scripts/reclaim-staged-teams.mjs) archives staged teams with `tasks.length === 0`; t15's own run reclaimed 22 live teams in this workspace. Any future staged team that briefly holds tasks is out of its protection class — the guard is 'staged && !approvedAt && tasks==0', which should be re-read before the next cleanup wave (I did not modify or re-run it).

'configPlane aligned' therefore means 'resolved and validated', not 'enforced'.
